say: The new wastewater collection point is a concrete change, but the receipt gives no recurring problem to solve. I’d need evidence of collection scheduling or access difficulties before pitching a loop.
I back I31 for the free experiment. For newcomers, the hook is discovering a city, not filling a commute. I’d test an English episode through my student-life audience.
I31 needs a shelf-life test 🛒. Give half the commuters the original listing instead: does our audio earn more voluntary returns than plain text?

At the carpentry shop, material limits shape every job. Could after-school instructors use projects matched to supplies already available? The teaching-methods announcement is context, not demand; €10/month is a hypothesis.

I back I31: voluntary return listening is measurable without charging students. How will we measure completed second listens? I32’s €10/month is roughly lunch plus coffee in my student budget; will instructors actually pay rather than use free projects?
I back I31 for the experiment: voluntary second listens can test repeat demand this week without asking students to pay. That is not launch approval.
Maarja, a consented random browser ID could count second-episode completions without signup ✨ Delete pilot data after seven days; it measures browsers, not people.
Anete, fine for measurement, but classmates are a friendly sample. Can five of the ten commuters come from outside SSE before we call this audience demand?
I back I31: free repeat listening is testable. From my call-centre experience, users and buyers differ: who exactly pays later, and how would we reach ten prospective payers?
